question: Should Christians pray in public?
summary: Matthew 6:5-6 explicitly forbids public prayer: do not be like the hypocrites who pray in synagogues and street corners to be seen — go into your inner room (*tameion*) and shut the door. John 11:41-42 has Jesus pray publicly at the tomb of Lazarus and explicitly say he did so 'because of the crowd standing around.' 1 Timothy 2:8 commands men to pray 'in every place' (*en panti topō*) lifting holy hands.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read Matthew's prohibition as targeting ostentatious motive, not public visibility, keeping it compatible with Jesus's tomb-side prayer and Paul's 'every place' command.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible catalogs Matthew's shut-door command against 1 Timothy's 'every place' and Jesus's own crowd-directed prayer as a flat contradiction.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/public.html

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's 'Doctrinal Discrepancies' chapter pairs Matt 6:5-6 directly against 1 Tim 2:8 (plus 1 Kings 8:22-23, 2 Kings 4:33, Dan 6:10-11, Luke 6:12, Acts 10:9) under the heading 'Prayer. May be in public. Should be in private,' concluding: 'It is not publicity, but ostentation in prayer, which is prohibited; not praying in public, but praying in conspicuous places to "be seen of men." The motive, not the place, is the thing in question.'

link.title: Is there a Bible contradiction in Matthew 6:6?
link.note: confirmed live; explicitly reconciles Matt 6:5-6 with Daniel's, Solomon's, and Paul's (1 Tim 2:8) public prayers via the same motive-not-place distinction

It may be offered in any circumstances, however open, if not prompted by the spirit of ostentation, but dictated by the great ends of prayer itself. It is the retiring character of true prayer which is here taught.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB's note states the prohibition targets ostentatious motive, not publicity itself — the exact distinction needed to reconcile Matt 6:5-6 with Jesus's crowd-directed prayer in John 11:41-42 and Paul's 'pray in every place' in 1 Tim 2:8.
